values: Logical sensors/actuators (subclasses of sosa:Sensor/Actuator) run SPARQL software procedures whose executions take observations as ssn:hasInput and produce observations as ssn:hasOutput; the door is both feature of interest and platform.

MCSO aligns to SSN mostly by equivalent classes (loose coupling); observations are grouped by DL-defined subclasses using usedProcedure to a campaign; sensor specifications (resolution, range) carry UO units.
ssn:Observation is aligned as a subclass of prov:Entity and orbac:Object, and sosa:hasResult as a subproperty of prov:generated, for usage-control policies on observations.

Actuators are linked to ssn:Properties through :PropertyChange and :Effect individuals, optimal conditions are OWL class expressions over properties, and Jena rules generate :Actions from actuator states; property values sit on property individuals.
The work mints its own terms in the ssn: namespace (ssn:isMotedBy, ssn:Kitchen, ssn:Mum, ssn:On) and refines ssn:isObservedBy into ssn:isSensedBy and ssn:isMotedBy per sensor kind.
Own terms are minted in the sosa: and owl: namespaces (sosa:hasOccuredAt, owl:hasObservationValue); rooms are platforms; results are activity labels used in SWRL/SQWRL rules.
Logical sensors/actuators (subclasses of sosa:Sensor/Actuator) run software procedures whose executions take observations as ssn:hasInput and produce observations as ssn:hasOutput.

Observations subclassed per quantity (ex:TemperatureObservation); the C-SPARQL queries re-mint SOSA properties in the work's anomaly: namespace (anomaly:hosts, anomaly:madeObservation, anomaly:hasSimpleResult).

Old SSN (ssnx) with observation subclasses per event type (?ob rdfs:subClassOf ssn:Observation); sensors are event services discovered by observed property and feature; location values are observation results.
Individual animals (southern elephant seals) are modelled as sosa:Platform hosting satellite tags; time, space and units are said to use OWL-Time, GeoSPARQL and QUDT but are not shown in data.

Alignment of the W3C Thing Description with SSN: things may be systems, platforms or features of interest, connected devices are modelled as features of interest, and property affordances relate to ssn:Property through ssn:forProperty, inferred from @type tags by rules.

Only SOSA properties are imported, not its classes; observations are subclassed into NumericObservation and StatusObservation, and sensors are linked by own correlation and influence properties for diagnosis.

Observations are workflow activity instances (vpd:SensorActivityInstance subclass of sosa:Observation and wild:ActivityInstance), sensor and machine activities are subclasses of sosa:Procedure, and DCAT datasets link to observations through prov:wasGeneratedBy.
Indoor-positioning observations of workers have locations as their values and are chained by dicp:hasNextObservation; observedProperty points to saref:Property in the SAREF alignment.

Observations are satellite images (sors:SatelliteImage equivalent to sosa:Observation) subclassed per satellite (LandsatImage, SentinelImage, MODISImage); results are subclassed per land-cover percentage.
Informal SSN-like triples with own property names (:observedBy, :observationValue, :time); the user's location is an observation value used by SWRL context rules.
Forecast models are virtual sensors; quantile predictions use 24 sub-properties of sosa:hasSimpleResult (covid-so:point, covid-so:quantile-N).
Old SSN (ssnx) with CF properties; sensors point to a per-plot feature with ssn:ofFeature, and plots link to crop treatments for filtering.
Cyber-twin ontology: machine automation programs and data translators are subclasses of sosa:Procedure, machines link to sensors, actuators and platforms by own properties.
An own observation-like class pdto:AtomicInformation links a product (pdto:hasFeatureOfInterest) and an ssn:Property (pdto:clarifiedProperty) to a value, instead of sosa:Observation.

Data-quality assessments are attached per observation through idqa:qualityOfObservation, a subproperty of ssn-system:qualityOfObservation, after SHACL validation; the IoT device collecting data is called a sosa:Sampler.
A hardware device is one wot:Thing typed both sosa:Sensor and sosa:Actuator; user preferences on WebThings properties are matched to actuators.
Knowledge base overlays merge a building knowledge base (SSN observations) with smartphone knowledge bases so that logical actuators use users' observations and preferences.
Observation classes defined by a value restriction on hasSimpleResult (ex:HighTempObservation) for anomaly classification; sosa:observes points to a unit.
Lightweight stream ontology: StreamObservation (sosa:Observation subclass) carries only values and timestamps, metadata (sensor, unit, quantity kind, location, service) sit on the IotStream.
Machine perception by abduction: ssn:isPropertyOf between properties and features (diseases) is encoded as a bit matrix to explain observed properties.

Detected anomaly events carry the detector as sosa:usedProcedure and point with ssn:wasOriginatedBy to the sensor properties whose time series triggered them; sensor metadata drive dashboard widget selection.
A SWRL rule types the sensor itself as the observation (Observation(?sensor)); SSN/SAN terms are reimported with own properties (hasSpot, hasState, hasValue) and converted to Drools rules.

A meta-context model mixing old SSN (ssn:Device, ssn:SensingDevice), IoT-Lite and an own iot-context vocabulary is populated by an LLM mapping table columns to concepts, to derive functional dependencies for data cleaning.
SOSA and QUDT terms appear as key-value pairs in Avahi (mDNS) service advertisements so that oneM2M devices discover each other without a controller.
Observations are deliberately kept out of the knowledge graph (BIM-IoTDI) to avoid growth; only sensors, properties and rooms are described semantically, with BOT, IFC and Brick.
Actors and human-centricity factors are linked directly to sensors by isObservedBy, and sensors send outputs to an own Data class, without sosa:Observation.

No observedProperty: the quantity is encoded in the observation IRI (urn:dev:mac:…/current, …/voltage), and a sosa:hasUnit term not in SOSA is invented; the JSON-LD serves as a baseline for CBOR templates.
Process steps and transformation processes are subclasses of sosa:Actuation, performed by sosa:Actuator (PO2:Material) with sosa:Procedure (PO2:Method); observations are attached to steps.
An AnonymizationProcedure subclass of sosa:Procedure records how personal information was removed; observations are mapped to access-control Resources.
Signals not produced by any sensor get a vss:VirtualSensor to fit the SOSA pattern; observations are abstracted into step:Episode instances of semantic trajectories by rules.
SSN classes (ObservableProperty, Sensor) are reimplemented as Python graph-object classes stored in Neo4j, with methods named after SSN properties.
Old SSN data published from a relational database with D2RQ mappings that generate both the sensor-type classes and the sensor instances.
RDF-star quoted triples are typed as observations (a frame image, detections, tracklets), each with sosa:usedProcedure pointing to the DNN or tracking algorithm (:Yolo, :KalmanFilter).
sosa:Observation and saref:Measurement are both aligned to an own Observation class; observations are checked against indoor-condition constraints of construction activities.
Old SSN ssn:SensingDevice linked by own properties (mmkg:outputs to data, mmkg:hasMeasuringProperty to an own MeasurementProperty class) in a multimodal scene graph; no sosa:Observation.
Observations are subclassed per type of sensor that generated them (four subclasses) and linked to recognised activities.
Numerical values are kept out of the ontology (time-series store); the ontology describes only measures, features and properties.
qb:Observation is declared equivalent to sosa:Observation, merging Data Cube and SOSA; O&M sampling points are subclasses of geosparql:Point.
Each sensor reading is an LDP RDF source typed ssn:SensorOutput served over CoAP, with no observation node.
SSN/SOSA device instances are combined with GDPRtEXT privacy-by-design concepts.
Old SSN sensors in a process-model knowledge base carry energy-cost attributes as literals containing the unit name, queried with a regex on "milliwatt".
A data acquisition system class (DAS) implements the procedure and is connected to sensors.
Smart musical instruments are platforms hosting sensors and also expose services.
Extends IoT-Stream (StreamObservation, IotStream with sosa:Sensor, QU quantity kind and unit, geo:Point) with patient and health-condition classes.
Observation events carry sensor and timestamp so that precise measurements are fetched from a time-series database on demand.
ssn:hasProperty links objects of video scenes (scene ontology) to their characteristics in a causal knowledge graph used for link prediction.
